newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's IMF forum to include leading speakers.
newsitem.headline: HK's IMF forum to include leading speakers.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Tuesday a major financial forum on March 7 will feature several central bankers from various countries. British Governor Chris Patten will kickoff the "Financial integration in Asia and the role of Hong Kong" conference, with Financial Secretary Donald Tsang giving the luncheon speech and International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus giving the keynote speech. UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, People's Bank of China governor Dai Xianglong and deputy governor Chen Yuan, Malaysian deputy prime minister Anwar Ibrahim, Goldman, Sachs & Co managing director Gerald Corrigan, Bank Indonesia governor Soedradjad Djiwandono, Bank of Korea governor K.S.Lee and Gabriel Singson of Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas were also among the featured speakers.
Hong Kong's Secretary for Financial Services Rafael Hui is also expected to speak.
The territory's future leader Tung Chee-hwa is slated to close the conference. The conference, is jointly organised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the International Monetary Fund.
